note: 'elonei means large trees (oaks or terebinths). "Plains" follows the Targum tradition.
The Masoretes pointed 'adonay as the divine title. I read it as Abraham's polite address to an unrecognised visitor ('adoni/'adonay "my lord/sirs"), which the plural verbs in v. 4 support.
chem'ah is curdled milk, like yogurt or soft cheese, not churned butter.

kjv: I will certainly return unto thee according to the time of life
mine: I will surely return to you about this time next year
note: ka'et chayyah means "at the time when it lives (again)", that is, when the season comes round. The KJV's literal "time of life" is opaque. Same in v. 14.

kjv: For I know him, that he will command his children
mine: For I have chosen him, so that he may command his children
note: yada' here means "chose, acknowledged" (cf. Amos 3:2), and lema'an 'asher is purposive ("in order that"). The KJV turns God's purpose into a prediction about Abraham's character.
